summary: V2 Phase A backend tests: 19/21 passed (90.5%). All wallet/expenses/vendors/estimates/BOQ/payment-flow/audit/executive/role-isolation/plan-enforcement endpoints work. The new attendance auto-credit-to-wallet flow is NOT implemented in the attendance handler - this is the only critical miss.

critical.issue: Handler in server.py (lines 554-569) only upserts attendance doc; it does NOT create labour_ledger EARNING entries or recompute_wallet. PRESENT/HALF/ABSENT statuses and legacy `present:true` both fail to auto-credit. Wallet snapshot stays at 0 earned even after marking PRESENT. This violates explicit Phase A requirement.

action_items: Implement attendance auto-credit in POST /api/attendance handler in /app/backend/server.py: for each entry, resolve labour, compute earning = daily_wage * ATTENDANCE_RATE[status] + overtime_hours*(daily_wage/8). Treat legacy `present:true` as status=PRESENT and `present:false` as ABSENT. Delete prior labour_ledger entries for (labour_id, site_id, date, type='EARNING') before inserting fresh ones to maintain idempotency. After all inserts, call recompute_wallet(labour_id) for each labour touched. Also log audit (MARK, attendance, attendance_doc_id).
Also handle `advance` field in attendance entries: optionally create ADVANCE ledger entry for that date.
Update server.py /api/subscription/upgrade prices from {PREMIUM:4999, ENTERPRISE:14999} to {PREMIUM:499, ENTERPRISE:1199} to match PLAN_PRICES in v2.py (currently inconsistent).
Optional: split server.py (964 lines) and v2.py (560 lines) into module folders for maintainability.
critical_code_review_comments: INCONSISTENT PRICING: server.py L734 has PREMIUM=4999/ENTERPRISE=14999 in /api/subscription/upgrade, but v2.py PLAN_PRICES is 499/1199. Frontend may show wrong amounts depending on which endpoint it hits.

server.py L222 `raise HTTPException(403, ...)` inside an `except jwt.PyJWTError` is fine, but `raise HTTPException(401, 'Invalid token')` should use `from None` or chain explicitly to avoid leaking trace.
v2.py recompute_wallet uses $in with PAYMENT/ADVANCE for paid total — correct, but BONUS is grouped with EARNING which is acceptable, just document.

server.py mark_attendance dictionary contains `_id` because doc is passed via $set after Motor inserts an _id field on dict mutation? No — `$set: doc` could inject created_at duplicates on upsert; consider stripping `id`/`created_at` from `$set` on subsequent upserts to keep original id.
CORS middleware added AFTER router include in server.py L811-822 — order is fine for Starlette but unusual; OK.
Files >700 lines: server.py is 964 lines, recommend splitting into routers/{auth,sites,labour,materials,payments,dashboard,ai}.py.

Only failures should be TestAttendanceWallet::test_attendance_status_creates_earning and test_legacy_present_true once main agent fixes attendance handler to auto-create labour_ledger EARNING entries. The fix must be idempotent (delete prior EARNING for same labour+date+site before re-inserting). rca of the issue: The attendance handler in /app/backend/server.py @api.post('/attendance') performs only an upsert on db.attendance. It does not iterate entries, does not look up labour daily_wage, does not write to db.labour_ledger, and never calls v2.recompute_wallet. Therefore wallet.balance always remains at whatever was set by explicit /api/wallet/pay calls only. To fix: after upsert, loop over body.entries, normalize status (legacy `present:true`->PRESENT, `present:false`->ABSENT), compute earning amount, delete prior matching EARNING entries (idempotent), insert new EARNING entries with date=body.date, then call recompute_wallet(labour_id) for each touched labour.
